caption: Piano: C major chord (C3 C4 E4 G4 C5), pianissimo (velocity 32), held 4.5 s then released
Piano: the same chord fortissimo (velocity 118) — brighter from the nonlinear felt, not just louder
Piano: A0 forte, held 9 s — inharmonic bass partials, phantom partials, long double decay
Piano: arpeggios C–F–G7–C with legato sustain pedalling; undamped strings ring sympathetically through the soundboard
Piano: a soft phrase with continuous half-pedal (CC64 ≈ 0.42) and una corda — notes blur partially and the third string of each trichord rings only sympathetically
Prepared piano: bolts, screws and rubber modelled as masses and dashpots on the strings (after Cage)
Violin: G major scale G3–G5, détaché bow strokes, string crossings chosen like a player would
Violin: a long E5 with vibrato and a bow-speed swell (CC11) — the Helmholtz motion grows and brightens
Violin: double stops G3+D4 and D4+A4, then a G-major triple stop — each note on its own string, all sharing one bridge and body
Viola: C3–G3 on the C string, then a C-major triple stop
Cello: C major arpeggio C2–C4 across all four strings; open strings answer sympathetically
Cello: a long G2 with vibrato, joined by D3 as a double stop
Flute: a legato phrase C5–G5 — fingering changes without re-tonguing, breath noise and vibrato
Flute: C4 and G4 (first register), C6 (overblown octave of C5), G6 (overblown twelfth of C5)
Flute: one fingering (D4) with breath pressure rising slowly — the jet speeds up, the tone brightens, then the tube jumps to its octave
All five instruments together (rendered separately, summed): piano chords with pedal, cello bass, viola and violin inner voices, flute melody
